entities.evidence: Abram, Terah’s son and later named Abraham, owns the livestock tended by the first group of herdsmen.
Lot, Haran’s son and Abram’s nephew, owns the livestock tended by the second group of herdsmen.
As in Genesis 12:6, the singular gentilic names the Canaanites collectively. Here they live in the land alongside the Perizzites.
The singular gentilic names the Perizzites collectively as a people living alongside the Canaanites.

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי רִיב introduces a quarrel as the next event in the narrative. The paired phrases בֵּין … וּבֵין identify the two parties, Abram’s herders and Lot’s herders.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to יְהִי, the shortened Qal wayyiqtol form, third person masculine singular. The verb agrees with רִיב, “a quarrel.”

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי רִיב means “a quarrel arose.” The paired phrases בֵּין … וּבֵין identify the two parties to the quarrel, Abram’s herders and Lot’s herders.
analysis.morphology: A singular absolute common noun of either gender, with no prefix or suffix. It is the subject of וַיְהִי.

analysis.evidence: After רִיב ‘quarrel’, בֵּין introduces Abram’s herders, and וּבֵין introduces Lot’s herders. The paired prepositions identify the two parties to the quarrel.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם means “those who tend Abram’s livestock.” The parallel phrase רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט identifies Lot’s herdsmen as the other party to the dispute.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine plural construct, used substantivally for those who tend livestock.

analysis.evidence: רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם means “the herders of Abram’s livestock.” The parallel phrase רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט identifies Lot’s herders as the other party to the dispute.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state. The following name אַבְרָם identifies the owner.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: The parallel phrases רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם and רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט identify the herders by whose livestock they tend. אַבְרָם names the owner of the first group’s livestock, just as לוֹט names the owner of the second group’s livestock.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct chain רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: The paired בֵּין … וּבֵין identifies the two parties to the רִיב (quarrel). The first בֵּין introduces Abram’s herders, and the marked וּבֵין introduces Lot’s herders.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ (and) is prefixed to the preposition בֵין (between).
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: In רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט, the participle identifies those who tend Lot’s livestock. The parallel phrase רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם identifies Abram’s herdsmen as the other party to the dispute.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine plural construct, used substantivally for the people who tend livestock.

analysis.evidence: רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט means “the herders of Lot’s livestock” and parallels רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם, “the herders of Abram’s livestock.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, with collective meaning. The following name לוֹט identifies the owner.

analysis.evidence: רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט means “the herders of Lot’s livestock.” It parallels רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה אַבְרָם, “the herders of Abram’s livestock.” Each name identifies the owner of the livestock.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It closes the construct chain רֹעֵי מִקְנֵה לוֹט.

analysis.evidence: The verse pairs הַכְּנַעֲנִי with הַפְּרִזִּי, the Perizzites, and says that both peoples were then living in the land.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ and definite article הַ precede a masculine singular absolute gentilic used collectively.

draft.change: Add the gentilic פְּרִזִּי under פרז and correct the occurrence gloss from “cup” to “and the Perizzites.”
draft.definition: A member of the Perizzite people. The definite singular can designate the people collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 13:7 names the Perizzites alongside the Canaanites as inhabitants of the land.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 13:7 pairs הַפְּרִזִּי with הַכְּנַעֲנִי, “the Canaanite.” The words אָז יֹשֵׁב בָּאָרֶץ describe both peoples as dwelling in the land at that time.
analysis.morphology: וְ means “and,” and הַ is the definite article. פְּרִזִּי is a masculine singular gentilic noun in the absolute state. The definite singular refers collectively to the people.
analysis.sense: The Perizzite people who lived in the land in Abram’s time.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68614:10, 66586:9.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew adverb with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אָז means “at that time,” and בָּאָרֶץ gives the place of residence. The clause says that the Canaanites and Perizzites were living in the land when the herders quarreled.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, used as the predicate of two coordinated collective singulars.
analysis.sense: to dwell habitually in a place

analysis.evidence: יֹשֵׁב בָּאָרֶץ says that the Canaanites and Perizzites were then living in the land. The noun denotes the territory they inhabited.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ ‘in’ incorporates the definite article in בָּ before א. The noun is common, of both genders, singular and absolute.
